issues.failure_explanation: The displayed formula contains two consecutive equality signs: the expression \max_{j \in [r]} = \sigma_j is syntactically malformed and mathematically undefined as written. The intended identity \TNorm{\matA} = \max_{j \in [r]} \sigma_j (i.e. the operator norm equals the largest singular value) is false in the written form because the equality with an empty right-hand side after \max_{j \in [r]} has no meaning.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious equality sign so the formula reads \TNorm{\matA} = \max_{j \in [r]} \sigma_j.
issues.overall_effect: The stated formula for the operator norm of a matrix is wrong as written. The surrounding context and the standard Eckart–Young relation make the intended correction discernible, so the downstream arguments that rely on the operator norm (e.g. the introductory matrix Eckart–Young statement) can be reconstructed.
issues.title: Formula for operator norm of matrix is malformed and incorrect as written
issues.why_classification: A single-character deletion of the spurious '=' restores the standard correct identity. No argument or guarantee needs to be reworked; the reader can see the forced correction directly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As a result, we have that the $\mm$-product is indeed a matrix-mimetic multiplication between tubal tensors.

issues.failure_explanation: The second identity property as written is $\tB \mm \tA = \tB$ for all $\tA, \tB$. This claims that left multiplication by any tensor $\tB$ always returns $\tB$, which is false. The correct two-sided identity property is $\tI \mm \tA = \tA$ and $\tA \mm \tI = \tA$. The definition is therefore mathematically incorrect as stated. Because the definition is invoked to assert that the $\mm$-product is matrix-mimetic and that the tSVDM exists, the written false property undercuts those claims as stated.

failure_location.quote: The \textbf{identity tensor} $\tI \in \FFF^{m \xx m \xx n}$ under $\mm$ is such that $\tI \mm \tA = \tA , \tB \mm \tA = \tB$ for all $\tA , \tB$ of compatible sizes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false equation $\tB \mm \tA = \tB$ with the correct right-identity equation $\tA \mm \tI = \tA$.
issues.overall_effect: The identity element of the $\mm$-product is defined by a false property. All constructions that rely on the stated identity behavior (the tSVDM, and results that use $\tQ^\CT \mm \tQ = \tI$) inherit an incorrect foundation as written, though the correct identity does exist and the properties can be repaired locally.
issues.title: Identity-tensor property states a false equation
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single-equation local fix inside a definition. The correct identity tensor exists and all downstream algebraic constructions are unchanged once the statement is corrected; no proof, algorithm, or guarantee needs to be rebuilt.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that $\RR_n$ exhibits Eckart-Young optimality (\Cref{def:optimality.prop}), then for any distinct $j,h \in [\ell]$ and $s \in \varsigma(j)$, $t \in \varsigma(h)$ it holds that $\matM_{s} \matM_{t}^\CT = 0$
\Cref{lem:nec.opt.disjoint.idempotent,lem:nec.opt.intra.idempotent.ortho} show that the rows of $\matM$ are pairwise orthogonal.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims that rows of $\matM$ associated with any two distinct idempotent components are orthogonal. The proof constructs a specific competitor tensor $\bs{a}$ using conjugate index pairs $s,s' \in \varsigma(j)$ and $t,t' \in \varsigma(h)$, then optimizes over $\beta_j \in \CC$ to derive $g_{s,t} = 0$. This construction requires $|\varsigma(j)| \geq 2$ and $|\varsigma(h)| \geq 2$, i.e. $d_j = 2$ and $d_h = 2$. When $d_j = 1$ or $d_h = 1$ (which happens whenever a principal ideal is isomorphic to $\RR$ rather than $\CC$), the set $\varsigma(j)$ is a singleton and no conjugate pair $s \neq s'$ exists. The proof's construction of $\bs{a}$ cannot be carried out and the optimization argument does not apply. No other argument is provided for these cases. Since the lemma's conclusion is needed in full generality to establish pairwise orthogonality of $\matM$'s rows in the proof of the main characterization theorem, the necessity direction of that theorem is unsupported for tubal rings with mixed real and complex principal ideals.

failure_location.quote: Assume then that $d_j =2$ and let $s, s' \in \varsigma(j)$ be the distinct indices associated with idempotent $\bs{e}_j$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the necessity argument to cover all cases $d_j, d_h \in \{1, 2\}$: for $d_j = 1$ or $d_h = 1$, construct an appropriate Frobenius-norm counterexample tensor (e.g. using $1 \times 1$ or $1 \times 2$ tubal tensors with a single unconstrained complex scalar in the optimizer) that yields the same orthogonality conclusion, or provide a uniform argument that does not rely on conjugate index pairs.
issues.overall_effect: The necessity direction of the main theorem (thm:necessary_sufficient_conditions_optimality) is incomplete: pairwise orthogonality of rows of $\matM$ across different idempotent components is proved only when both components have $d = 2$. The characterization of Eckart-Young-optimal transforms therefore lacks a complete proof for tubal rings containing both real ($d=1$) and complex ($d=2$) principal ideals, and for tubal rings with only real principal ideals.
issues.title: Proof of cross-idempotent row orthogonality covers only the d_j = d_h = 2 case
issues.why_classification: The gap requires a nontrivial additional argument (a new counterexample construction and optimization for the mixed and real cases) but does not require new global proof architecture. The main theorem's statement and its sufficiency direction are unaffected; only the necessity proof is incomplete. A contained extension of the existing technique would close the gap without changing the characterization, the framework, or any guarantee.
